core.title: Resolve every flow router participant and lifeline
core.given: A plan artifact contains a flow router that lists participants and lifelines
core.when: The plan is authored, revised or checked
core.then: Every participant and lifeline the flow router lists is either an external actor or a typed reference to an artifact the plan declares.
prefer: Declare the missing participant as an artifact in the plan and reference it with a typed reference.
Correct a lifeline that points at the wrong, an undeclared, or an untyped target.
avoid: Routing decisions between participants the plan does not declare.
Free-text or untyped participant/lifeline names, even when a matching artifact exists.
core.why: A routing decision between participants the plan does not declare cannot be traced to anything that implements it.
evidence: The stack's plan-integrity check passes for the plan with respect to flow router participants and lifelines.
Each participant/lifeline is either an external actor or a typed reference whose target is declared in the same plan.
verification: Realized by a plan-integrity check over plan artifacts. It examines every participant and lifeline in each flow router (not only changed ones): an entry passes only if it is an external actor (per the profile's external-actor syntax) or a typed reference resolving to an artifact the plan declares.
The check covers only flow router participants and lifelines; other plan content is out of its scope.
The check never scans vendored and generated trees; the exact excluded trees are the profile's one stack-wide excluded-roots list.

values: plan artifact containing a flow router
a plan-integrity check reports a participant or lifeline that is neither an external actor nor a typed reference to an artifact the plan declares

fires: Any participant a flow router lists that is neither an external actor nor a typed reference to an artifact the plan declares — including untyped/free-text names, whether or not a matching artifact exists.

Any lifeline a flow router lists that is neither an external actor nor a typed reference to an artifact the plan declares — including untyped lifelines whose intended target exists, and typed references whose target is not declared in the plan.
Existing, unchanged flow routers in a plan that violate the invariant (the rule applies to every listed participant and lifeline, not only edited ones).
doesNotFire: Every participant and lifeline of every flow router is either an external actor or a typed reference whose target artifact is declared in the same plan.
The file sits in a vendored or generated tree the stack never scans (the profile's excluded roots).

profileRequirements.meaning: The syntax by which a plan artifact names an external actor; the core's obligation and evidence say 'external actor' and the profile supplies the concrete prefixes.
Vendored and generated trees that the check never scans (one stack-wide list).

bunOnly.text: Package rule, strict: a rule of this package's own gates (`atdd-bun.*`), realized by a package guard rather than a canonical planner node; held to the same per-rule checks as every convention: a convention, strict, a failing fixture, relationship edges.
bunOnly.reason: ATDD-Bun package-governance metadata (the `atdd-bun.*` gate namespace and its package-guard realization); it describes how the ATDD-Bun distribution governs its own rules and has no stack-neutral equivalent. The strict disposition it repeats is carried by core:verification via verifier_detail[2].

neutralityNotes: The obligation itself is stack-neutral; only the external-actor prefixes (`user:…`, `system:…`) were concrete, and they are moved to the proposed profile key idiom.plan_syntax#external_actor (pending owner approval) — until approved the Bun prefixes live only in the realization and the worked reference. The activation fact 'plan artifact containing a flow router' is a rule-specific semantic predicate that stays in core activation with needs_new_observer observability; bun.json names no concrete artifact kind playing the plan-artifact role, so no roles.plan_artifact.kinds profile requirement is claimed and each realization's observer defines which files count as plan artifacts. bun.json never spells out the typed-reference syntax either, so the core keeps 'typed reference' as the neutral term and each realization defines what counts as typed; this makes the core neither weaker nor stronger. The path_glob fact has no neutral fact type and is a scan exclusion rather than an authoring waiver, so it is carried in core:verification plus roots.excluded. Severity 3 and strict disposition are kept in core:verification per the vocabulary's notProfileKeys. The validator id and the ATDD-Bun package-governance text (verifier_detail[3]) have no neutral equivalent and are bunOnly. 'unless' is empty in bun.json and stays empty.
